record.context_brief: Lozenge tilings of a hexagon with one central triangular hole
record.original_question: Find an exact formula for the number of lozenge tilings of the hexagon with side lengths n, n+1, n, n+1, n, n+1 after deleting the central triangle.

evidence.quote: The hexagon of side-lengths n, n + 1, n, n + 1, n, n + 1 cannot be tiled by lozenges at all, for in the dissection into unit triangles, the number of upward-pointing triangles differs from the number of downward-pointing triangles. However, if one removes the central triangle, one gets a region that can be tiled, and the sort of numbers one gets for small values of n are striking.
Problem 2: Enumerate the lozenge-tilings of the region obtained from the n, n + 1, n, n + 1, n, n + 1 hexagon by removing the central triangle.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider, in the plane triangular lattice, a hexagon with successive side lengths $n, n+1, n, n+1, n, n+1$ (with all interior angles equal to $120^\circ$). Dissect this hexagon into unit equilateral triangles. Because the number of upward-pointing unit triangles differs by one from the number of downward-pointing unit triangles, the hexagon itself admits no tiling by lozenges (unit rhombi with $60^\circ$ and $120^\circ$ angles, each covering exactly one upward and one downward unit triangle). Remove the single unit triangle located at the center of the hexagon; the resulting region $R_n$ has equal numbers of upward and downward unit triangles, and is tileable by lozenges. Let $T(n)$ denote the number of lozenge tilings of $R_n$. Find a closed-form (product) formula for $T(n)$ valid for all positive integers $n$.
artifact.category_tag: Lozenge tilings of hexagons with holes
artifact.status_search_result: The enumeration problem was solved independently by M. Ciucu (1998, using his Matchings Factorization / "factorial" theorem giving a product formula in terms of self-complementary plane partition counts) and by H. Helfgott and I. Gessel (1999, "Enumeration of Tilings of Diamonds and Hexagons with Defects"). Both works provide explicit product formulas for the number of lozenge tilings of the (n,n+1,n,n+1,n,n+1) hexagon with its central unit triangle removed.

status_evidence.title: Enumeration of Lozenge Tilings of Hexagons with a Central Triangular Hole
status_evidence.snippet: Ciucu's paper enumerates lozenge tilings of hexagons with a central triangular hole, giving closed-form product formulas.
status_evidence.claim: Ciucu provided a closed-form enumeration for the lozenge tilings of the hexagon with central triangular hole, solving Propp's problem.

status_evidence.title: Enumeration of Tilings of Diamonds and Hexagons with Defects
status_evidence.snippet: Helfgott and Gessel enumerate tilings of diamonds and hexagons with defects, including the n,n+1,... hexagon with central triangle removed.
status_evidence.claim: Helfgott and Gessel independently gave a product formula for this enumeration.
